newsitem.title: USA: Showers to continue across US Midwest - forecasters.
newsitem.headline: Showers to continue across US Midwest - forecasters.

text.p: A fast-moving system produced 0.75 to 2.0 inches of rain the past 24 hours from central Iowa across northern Illinois, and a second system due late Thursday should track further south, meteorologists said.
"Basically, the entire central U.S. (will receive rain), 1/2 to 1-1/2 inches will be common amounts," said Fred Gesser, Weather Express Inc meteorologist, referring to coverage by the second system.
Gesser said the rain should miss an area from southwest Kansas to the Texas Panhandle.

He expects more rain Monday and Tuesday beginning in the central Plains Monday and moving into the Midwest Tuesday. Rain amounts of 0.10 to 0.75 inch were likely with greatest amounts along the northern edge of that path.
Cool weather should remain in the Midwest until Tuesday, when Gesser expects a warmup for the rest of the week.
"I think temperatures will normalize in the western Corn Belt Tuesday and Wednesday and hold through the weekend," he said.

Weather Services Corp meteorologist Joel Burgio forecast a warmup in the Midwest Monday and Tuesday, but below normal temperatures should return to the western Midwest Wednesday and eastern areas Thursday.
"You will have one or two days of normal to above normal temperatures before it cools off," he said.
Also, the National Weather six- to 10-day outlook released Wednesday for several Midwest states indicated below normal temperatures and above normal rainfall.
WSC's Burgio forecasted a cold weekend for southwest Kansas to the northern Texas Panhandle with lows near freezing Saturday night and Sunday morning.
"That probably is not damaging (to the wheat). It would need to be heading or flowering to be damaged," he said of the cold weather.
Light, scattered showers were forecast for spring wheat areas through early next week. But Burgio, said the wet soils from recent flooding will delay spring planting more than the scattered showers.
